My family and I head off into the woods with water filters, plenty of canned foods and surplus fuel. In a desperate attempt to find food and water, our family packs up to leave, but get stuck on the road from backed up traffic. As a social animal, killing each other is, for the most part, destructive to us functioning as a social unit. The traditional source of human meat has been dead humans, and dead humans tend to come from living humans who become dead. Those who become dead by murder feed murderers who might survive another meal but wont find a fixed spot among a stable social species. Even a cannibal who normally practises through consent is less trustworthy in a dire situation than a normal person, seeing as there is something to gain from your death which normal people would not even consider until after you die. At that, those who become dead by nature tend to be a bad source of food, and those natural healthy deaths are scarce enough that an exception to the rule is not really made. Also add to the fact that eating some parts of ones own species actually causes problems (the shakes) to what could be seen as a natural deterrent.

"Morally wrong" is a very subjective thing, but there may be reasons that inform why these general commonplace morals arose.

The disgust reflex might also be more powerful in some than in others, and even being presented with synthetic human flesh could trigger the response, the reason does not have to be logical, just powerful enough to prevent them from eating 'destructive' things.

There are a lot of things where is it really hard to pinpoint immorality about an act. Objectively, cannibalism does no real harm ( except Kuru ) if the victim is already dead by a natural means. But, that doesn't mean that people don't recoil at the thought of being eaten or seeing a loved one eaten. We tend to view the things we eat as lower beings and to think of ourselves being reduced to the level of animals is abhorrent.

There are a lot of things that really don't have any perceivable societal harm but people still view them as taboo/immoral. Incest really harms no one if it is consensual and protection is used. Homosexuality harms no one and is arguably a societal good. The same can be said of prostitution. Even behaviors as extreme as coprophagia don't really harm anyone, but most people would view them as taboo/immoral.

Cannibalism just falls into a category of being one of those thing that offends the senses and makes people recoil at the thought.

Humans have both an overwhelming fear of death and an overly developed empathy system. The two sometimes conflict and any reminders about the death of someone with empathetic bonds, triggers the death fears of the self. Cannibalism is just a special case of this and adds the notion that humans might not be as removed from the food chain as we like to believe. It also produces a morbid curiosity. This may also be why Vampire Shows, Zombie movies, and Discovery Channel's Shark Week is so popular- even when people are more likely to be bitten by a human in New York than an actual shark.

This is that our souls and the white matter in our skulls have many of the same capabilities, but different responsibilities in a manner similar to how a pilot and autopilot have some similar capabilities, but different responsibilities. For example, a pilot chooses the path his vehicle will take and after a while can turn autopilot on and have the machine execute his plan. Certain ideas carry their own authority. Love each other and the golden rule, for example, which no spiritually mature person can argue. You ask if souls exist? Do you exist? The question is answered affirmatively by the very fact that you ask it. You are self aware. Therefore, you exist.

However, the existence of a life after this life is provable. I am certain of it. However, I know nothing more about that future life, comparative speaking, that I knew about this life when I was in my mother’s womb.

As we look at this life, we are all dwelling in organic machinery, bodies, which wear out. However, some thoughts never wear out. They can live in as many minds as they are given a home, and can be passed from intellect to intellect. When a teacher dies, what you learned as their student does not die with them. It lives in you. So if a thought can be immortal, we are too, since we produce those thoughts. The temporary cannot create the eternal, so our existence must go on in another form.

The organic machinery you currently dwell in began thusly: Two seeds united in the womb of your mother. There was a division after the union. The placenta received everything first. It placed itself between you and mother and gorged itself. But a small amount survived to reach you. Suddenly, you were born and the placenta was discarded as trash. You have never missed your self-centered placenta.

Now you are in here, dwelling in the organic machine that survived the womb – your body. And like the placenta that preceded it, your body gets everything first. All of us are born receiving. We do not give. But slowly the seed of our physical body begins to consider joining itself to the spiritual seed of “love each other”. The idea we should do so carries its own authority and no religion is needed to know the truth of it. Some take that love to heart. If you do, then just like the union in your mother’s womb that created the machinery you dwell in, so it is that union of the two seeds of body and love also create a pregnancy. At this point there is a division within you, just like in the womb. This time it is spiritual. You begin to see things differently. The selfishness must end. The concept of “we” becomes as important as “I”. There will be a slow growth within you that eventually makes this life too small, just as the womb became too small. And all the super rich and cruelly powerful, who have heaven on earth while you live off their scraps, so it is that they are your current placenta for your physical sustenance, while love feeds your mind that can bear less and less with those selfish demons raping the world and its inhabitants.

When you die this time, your body, which received everything first, just like your placenta once did, will suddenly be discarded, just as your placenta once was. You will never miss it. The next life will hold as much exponential growth compared to this life, as this life did compared to the virtual nothing you began here as.

Will it be perfect? No. Growing forever is how it must be when death has no power. But it will be happier.

Life goes on and on.
